title: THE ART OF A DYNAMIC TEACHER

sense.text:
This is the art of becoming a dynamic teacher. Dynamic means energetic, spirited, lively, vigorous, forceful, powerful, bold, passionate, fiery, full of get up and go: everything the people witnessed in the blitz at the 2819 church, a dynamic blitz full of dynamic teachers. And it starts here: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.”

You receive a good understanding when you are doing his commandments. That is the key to acquiring, learning and gaining understanding, and to teaching it as well.

precepts.why:
“Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” Israel was a wise and understanding people because they feared God and kept his commandments.

“For what nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them”, and “what nation is there so great, that hath statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day?” That is what made us great, not skin color. The people of Israel in the Bible were people of color, black, brown, different shades of brown, and melanin is a blessing in itself. But we do not teach that you get the kingdom because you are black. That is what they push out there to negate the message. Christianity is the one about race and color: a white Jesus, white prophets, white angels, and everyone in a biblical movie is Caucasian.

What made us great is that we came from great men and women, Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebecca, Jacob, Leah, Rachel, Joseph, descendants who kept the same laws that Moses brought back to us when we came out of Egypt. When people fear what they do not understand, they minimize it, because they cannot explain it or speak against it. That is a heathen tactic, whether Arab or white: the opposition minimizes what is greater than themselves.

sense.text: “A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear.” That prophet is Christ.

“This is he, that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel which spake to him in the mount Sina”: that was Christ talking to Moses. “And with our fathers: who received the lively oracles to give unto us.”

One of the words for dynamic was lively. The lively oracles are the laws of God; God calls them lively, and they were given unto us.

precepts.why:
“What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?” “Much every way.” There is a complete and utter advantage in being a Jew and being circumcised, in every way. Paul said it; the Bible does not say being a Jew is no advantage at all. Being an Israelite is an advantage because you come from a chosen line of people, so it does play a part in salvation, because salvation is only promised to the children of Israel, and that's it.

“Chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.” The same lively oracles of Acts 7 were committed unto us, and us alone, no one else. The commitment was for us to apply and to teach those lively commandments.
“A man of understanding trusteth in the law; and the law is faithful unto him, as an oracle.” The laws of God are faithful unto us as an oracle. The laws of God are our oracle: the lively oracles.

sense.text:
“If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God.” If any man is to teach this Bible, he has to use the Bible. Countless times the so-called elders and leaders outside of here will sit on an interview or on YouTube two or three hours straight with no Bible, no scripture, no verses, no chapters, just talk, just ranting. That is not what the Bible says to do.

You must speak the words in the Bible, not your own opinion or feelings or your own insults and ad hominems. You're a Caucasian, you're the devil; you're an Arab, you're a heathen: that's nice, but Bible. Whenever the Bishop, who is also a dynamic teacher, does an interview, he sits with a Bible in hand or in his lap and a reader on standby. The deacons were trained the same way by their elders: always a Bible in front of you or a reader with a Bible. We are not orphans here; we have elders that guide us.

“If any man minister, let him do it as of the ability which God giveth: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ.” When you are just talking and the Bible is not being used, there is no glory to God in that. Anything outside of that is confusion and misguidance.

precepts.why:
“These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” They received the word of the apostles with all readiness of mind, paying attention, and then searched the scriptures.

When Paul and them taught, they taught the Bible so as to force the people to search the scriptures daily to see if what they heard was real. If a man talks for two or three hours and the Bible is never used, can you search that in the Bible? No. You cannot find a man's words in the Bible; you find God's words there, and God's words are what the teacher should be speaking. That is what a dynamic teacher does: he uses the Bible so the people can go and see whether the things he read are true. Teaching by your own words and insults is not scriptural. It shows a lack of being a teacher; it is a novice tactic.

sense.text:
“For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God.” The oracles of God are the word of God, the laws of God, the lively oracles.

“And are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.” When you first come into this truth you are born again: you must learn to walk again, talk again, see, think, speak and learn again, as a babe all over again. So you must start off nourished with milk. You cannot feed a newborn child meat; they will choke and die on it. The meat comes when you are grown, have your teeth and have learned to chew. The meat is the deep understanding of the Bible: the deep sayings, the prophecies, the commandments and laws, and knowing how to apply them.

“For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.” Whoever is still on milk is still learning and is not ready to teach. You have to be nourished with the milk first before going out and teaching; otherwise you are unskilful in the word of righteousness. You can't put an infant on the ground and tell him to walk; it don't make no damn sense. He will lay there and cry. A babe will talk and not use a Bible. That is a babe, and a babe cannot teach. Sit down, learn and watch class.

“But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age”: the grown, those who have learned, gained experience, and acquired wisdom through growth and application. “Even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” By reason of constant use: experience, time, trial and error. You get up, you fall; you make your mistakes, but you rise again and become better. That is how the senses are exercised.

Watch a baby learn to walk. He falls and cries and tries again until his legs are strong enough; he stands scared, wobbles, takes one step and then another, and before you know it he is running around the house destroying everything, because he has exercised his senses and grown. You can't expect a newborn to walk right away. But some in the community of Israel are not elders, they are orphans: fearful, weak, lying, degenerate, no scriptures, no solutions, just talk. That's a babe.

precepts.why:
This is where Hebrews gets senses exercised to discern both good and evil. “And further, by these, my son, be admonished”: by these, the commandments. “Of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.” Don't be focused on a whole bunch of books. The Bible always is, should be and shall be the primary source.

“Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” That is the conclusion of the whole Bible, and the first thing read in Psalms 111:10: you gain wisdom by fearing God and keeping his commandments. That is man's role.

“For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” God shall bring every action of man and woman into judgment. We discern both good and evil by keeping the laws of God, and we will be judged on things good or evil. That is how our senses are exercised to discern both good and evil.

sense.text:
David wrote this psalm when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had committed adultery with Bathsheba and had her husband Uriah killed to take her as his wife. After Nathan confronted him, he wrote this, so everything in it comes after that confrontation.

“Create in me a clean heart, O God”: forgive me, Lord. His heart was unclean when he had the man killed and got her pregnant; David was moving crazy. “And renew a right spirit within me”: David's right spirit was gone when he did that. Men are fallible. Men fall, and they rise again if the Lord so chooses, or they fall forever.
“Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” Do not give me a reprobate mind for what I have done, and do not remove your holy spirit from me because of it.
“Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation”: restore it, because he lost it. “And uphold me with thy free spirit.”

“Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” Did the Lord say, David, you made a mistake, you fell, you can't teach no more? No. Once he was restored, then he would teach transgressors. Because David learned from his mistake and taught from it, that made him a dynamic teacher.

To become a dynamic teacher you must go through trials, and through those trials you will make mistakes; you will rise and you will fall. That is the making of a dynamic teacher: trial and error. No man is perfect. To use a man's fall against him is ridiculous; the question is whether he is better afterwards. David was better afterwards, Peter was better afterwards, all twelve were better afterwards except Judas, who killed himself. You can't answer someone bringing out scriptures this year by bringing up what happened with them three or four years ago. That doesn't work. Personal attacks don't work over here; you have to use the Bible.

David said that once a right spirit was restored he would teach transgressors, and sinners would be converted. “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness”: lay it aside, stop doing it. “And receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.”

The 2819 church says the law can't save you. That is not what James said. He said the engrafted word is able to save your souls. The commandments do save souls.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” If you are a doer of the word, it saves your soul. The people in Christianity believe they don't have to keep any laws at all, only hear the word and not do it, because they have been deceived. Christianity is a self-deceiver: I'm saved, I'm delivered, I got a personal relationship with God. How do you know? Where did you get that from? Deceiving your own selves.

“For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass.” He reads the Bible, which is a mirror. “For he beholdeth himself”: he sees himself in the scriptures. “And goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was”: he closes the Bible and forgets what he read, because he is not applying it. Just hearing and not doing is looking in the mirror and forgetting the reflection.

“If ye love me, keep my commandments.” We said this over and over at the blitz, and the people of that cult, Christianity, were furious. They stood in line by the tens of thousands, and we stood across the street on a public street with the mic, so they had to stand there and take it. Their pastor told them not to film inside, and inside was nothing but loud music and waving phones: a religious concert. Then on their way home they had to walk by us and get blasted again.

One Edomite prostrated himself on the hot ground and started praying for us, so fat you couldn't tell his front from his back, red skin burnt all over, until his wife told him to get up because he was embarrassing her. That is exactly where he belongs, but not yet: that is the kingdom. Right now he is symbolizing us: that is us in captivity.

“And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever.” Christ gives the stipulation: if you are keeping his commandments, he will pray the Father to give you another comforter. “Even the Spirit of truth”: the comforter is the spirit of truth, which is Christ himself, speaking of himself in the third person. “For he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you”: for now he dwells with you, but once he is gone his spirit will dwell in you.

“I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” He is that comforter of verse 16, that spirit of truth of verse 17. “At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.”

“He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father.” You must keep his commandments to show that you love him. Out there they were saying, I have a personal relationship with God. If you love God, you are keeping his commandments; a relationship with God is keeping his commandments. That is what he said in red letters.

“If a man love me, he will keep my words.” He says it numerous times: a man who loves him or wants a relationship with him and his Father will keep his words, not be a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is the same thing James said. “And my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.” Their spirit will abide in you. The Holy Spirit is the spirit of the Father and his Son in you.

“He that loveth me not keepeth not my sayings.” If you do not love God or have a relationship with him, you will not keep his commandments. The words Christ taught were not his own: they were Moses' words, which his Father taught him, and he taught them unto us.

“These things have I spoken unto you, being yet present with you”: while I am still here alive with you, because eventually I will be gone, but my spirit will remain in you if you keep my commandments, along with my Father's.

“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost”: Christ himself is the Holy Ghost, the spirit of his Father and him abiding in you. When you keep the commandments they dwell in you; when you do not, they don't. “He shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.” Because we were going to go into captivity and forget who we were until that spirit entered into us again, and here we are today. He told us these things before, when we were here before.

This is about conversion: the word that is able to save your souls, and David saying he would teach transgressors so sinners would be converted. “Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him”: if you make a mistake like David did, you fall, but you rise again and you rise better. And one corrects him or her.

“Let him know, that he which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.” He that converts the sinner is the teacher. That makes you a savior. Shout out to Captain Gal, who pulled this scripture.

When you were out there teaching at the 2819 church, even giving out a flyer or answering a question, you may have saved a soul from death and gotten them mercy. They may have walked away saying, I don't believe that, but you put the thought in their mind; you planted the seed, and one day the Most High will water it and they will come in. We threw seeds out there for hours. The harvest is plenty but the laborers are few, but not for long.

It was tactical, too. Right now the Israelis are under fire; everyone is speaking against Israel, the land, and the Israelis, the Zionists, Netanyahu, AIPAC, Canary Mission and the ADL are under complete scrutiny. While that is going on we are marching and teaching our people, and they can't say a word. It is the perfect season; the Most High God moved our spirit to do it. To hide a multitude of sins means they get mercy for their sins and repent from them.

Christ in John 14 was not saying something different from the Old Testament; he was repeating himself. “Wisdom crieth without”: wisdom cries outside. The prophets taught at the gates, in public; they were public speakers. “She uttereth her voice in the streets.” That is where we are now. Now Christian pastors are trying to mimic it with street preaching, because their pulpits and stadiums are not effective enough. We are having an effect on this world. The Lord does not show us all of it, because we would get arrogant and high-minded, but he gives a glimpse that what we are doing is effective. It's dynamic.

“She crieth in the chief place of concourse”: in the chief place where our people are found, you will find the prophets teaching. “In the openings of the gates: in the city she uttereth her words.” Not behind a pulpit, not in a building, but in the streets, in the concourse, in the city. And they are her words, not yours. Her words are the lively oracles of God. You speak Bible; you don't stand on a corner ranting and railing about what you feel, throwing insults. That is not Bible.

“How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity?” Wisdom will say to the people, how long will you be stupid? Wisdom can be insulting and offensive. Simple means stupid, dumb. How long will you love stupid things like Christianity, Catholicism, denominational or non-denominational doctrine, Islam, atheism, politics and sports?

“And the scorners delight in their scorning”: making fun of us. They call us Power Rangers. That doesn't offend us; it encourages us, because Power Rangers have power. We'll be the purple rangers. “And fools hate knowledge?”

“Turn you at my reproof”: repent, turn to the teaching at her reproof. “Behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you”: when you turn to the words of wisdom, he pours his spirit, that comforter, into you. “I will make known my words unto you”: once the spirit is in you, he makes his words known unto you. Like a newborn babe, who cannot speak until he grows, it is a process. But first you must turn to the words being taught in the streets, in the concourse, without and not within. Even when there was a pulpit, it was outside.

Read again: “For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.” When you have not yet learned how to apply the laws and commandments of God, you are still a babe with no experience, still crawling, swaddled in a blanket. You cannot teach like that; you have to grow first, by trial and error, rising and falling like an infant does.

Children are teachers too. They have no malice and they forgive: a child says you're mean, daddy, and is back in your arms within seconds. That is why Christ said to be converted and become as a little child. A lot of our people are vengeful, hateful, jealous, egotistical, arrogant and high-minded, or fearful, weak and cowardly, and you cannot be a dynamic teacher with those attributes. The Lord can't use you.

“But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” What gives that understanding is the Holy Spirit: the right spirit David asked not to be removed from him in Psalms 51, the same spirit poured out when you turn at wisdom's reproof in Proverbs 1:23.

“For the word of God is quick”: no matter how fast you run or where you hide, headphones and all, it is going to find you. “And powerful”: Power Rangers, right? “And sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow”: it hurts you physically and spiritually.

It is so powerful that people who can't stand us and hate our guts are in the comments watching class and taking notes. Why are you here? Something keeps drawing you. That is the word of God being used; it cuts people so bad they get mad, but they have to admit he ain't lying.

“And is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” We are not pointing fingers, but the word of God is so quick, precise and concise that what we bring out is them, and it offends them. Pull Romans 1 about same sex, they're mad. Christ is a black man, they're mad. Keep the commandments, they're mad. Don't be a whoremonger, don't be a fornicator: oh, you guys are judging. I wasn't talking to you; what are you mad about? Call it out and they're mad. Why? Because they're hoes. If you're not a hoe, you shouldn't be mad about it. A hit dog will holler. The word cuts them as they walk by; they turn their headphones all the way up, and the Most High kills the headphones just in time. The word of God is quick and always on time.

When you use it properly you see its power: someone says nothing but right, sis, and she gives him the finger, because whatever was said before cut her. A dynamic teacher can edify the crowd in the front while cutting the scorners and scoffers in the middle and the back; he can teach and blast at the same time, heal and hurt at the same time, heal with the sword and cut with the sword at the same time. Being surgical and precise takes dedication, time and leadership. You don't acquire that skill in an orphan camp. Elders were always a necessity in the Bible: either the elder was an elder or the elder had elders. No one is an island.

“For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal.” We are not advocating guns, missiles, grenades or firearms of any kind; we don't promote that at all. But this truth is warfare: we are fighting for the lives of our people, because Satan has our people in prison, called Christianity, politics, religion. We are at war with the devil himself and his children.

We didn't march out there with guns or knives or promote violence; we marched and did cadences. Even people who were there said so in the comments: be mindful of your words, they did not storm State Farm Arena, they did not attack us, they did not bombard us, they marched for their cause and stayed on the other side of the street. People were amazed at what they saw: young and older black and Hispanic men, the same people, in line, in step, in order, saying, believing and teaching the same thing. That's what black men need. We have all the footage.

“But mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds.” Our works, our actions, our dynamic teachings are mighty through God. Christianity, the 2819 church, is a stronghold that must be pulled down. We sit down with the Muslims all the time; the Nation of Islam invites us to speak at black gatherings. Their Islam is a false doctrine and their Allah is wrong, but they teach that we are the Israelites and that Christ is black, and there is respect despite the differences. But the Christianity cult pastors won't sit down with us. They are white supremacists in black skin, so we're coming for them.

“Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God.” We have to cast down imaginations. Pastor Pam is a disciple of Christian nationalism, which is religious white supremacy; his talking points come word for word from the white man who pushes white supremacist Christianity, and we have the videos.

“And bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ”: by force, through the word of God; compel them to come in, as Christ said.

“And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.” When you are no longer a babe and your obedience is fulfilled, you are ready to go out and teach, ready to revenge all disobedience through the power of God without weapons of any kind. The word of God is enough for us.
“And while he yet spake, behold a multitude, and he that was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them, and drew near unto Jesus to kiss him.” This is when they came to apprehend Christ.
“Lord, shall we smite with the sword?” Shall we act? They were ready to defend Christ from being locked up.

“And one of them smote the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.” That shows precision: the skill to cut off a man's right ear willfully without cutting off his whole head. That was a physical sword.
“Suffer ye thus far”: that's enough, stop. “And he touched his ear, and healed him”: Christ put the ear back on and healed it.

precepts.why:
Who cut that ear off with such precision? “Then Simon Peter having a sword drew it, and smote the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.” Peter pulled the sword out of the sheath and knew exactly what he was doing. Peter was a problem; he was a swordsman.

These men weren't regular. They didn't run and cower in danger like the orphan camps, who scatter and are nowhere to be found when gunshots ring out and their comrades are stabbed to death in the street. We don't do that here. If a man is found a coward here he is demoted immediately; cowardice keeps no rank. The disciples were precise with the sword of God, the word of God, and they were warriors physically also.

sense.text:
“For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtil.” Subtle goes back to quick: the word of God hits and you don't see it coming; it just happens, indirect. “Lively”: like the lively oracles.

“Clear, undefiled, plain.” The word of God is clear and plain. Christ being a black man and dying for his people is plain. Christianity makes what is clear and plain symbolic, metaphorical, allegorical, mystical, magical. “Loving the thing that is good”: loving the commandments, which are good. “Quick”: the word of God is quick. “Which cannot be letted”: it cannot be stopped, no matter what you do.

“Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care.” Free from care means it is not scared, not worried, not asking what we are going to do because we are making the white man mad. “Having all power, overseeing all things”: there is guidance, leadership, elders involved. The Peter Pan camps out here are lost boys with no guidance and no elders.

“Pure, and most subtil, spirits.” Wisdom itself is a spirit, and it says spirits, plural: there are different spirits of administration, some that teach, some that build, some that decorate, some that clean and maintain, all ministering to the congregation and working together as one for one goal, the benefit of the children of Israel.

“And if a man love righteousness her labours are virtues: for she teacheth temperance”: to maintain your calm, your cool. “And prudence”: wisdom. “Justice”: the Bible teaches real justice. Black folks are the most forgiving people on earth: they gun us down and hang us, and we forgive because Jesus is white. When Botham Jean was killed in his own apartment by Amber Guyger, his brother gave her a hug, the judge gave her a hug and a Bible, and the court officer combed her hair. No wisdom. Justice is God's vengeance: he that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity, he that lives by the sword must die by the sword. Outside of that is feelings and emotions, Barney and Sesame Street, not Bible.

“And fortitude.” Fortitude is courage in pain or adversity: bravery, strength of mind and of character, moral strength, toughness of spirit, firmness of purpose, resilience, backbone, spine, mettle, nerve, fearlessness, valor, stoutheartedness, endurance, steadfastness, patience, longsuffering, tenacity, perseverance, resolve, determination, guts, grit. From the Latin, strength, force, firmness, manliness. Wisdom gives you all those attributes. Some of these Israelites and pastors lack testicular fortitude on the highest level.

It is emphasized because, as was said weeks ago, a time will come when the Israelites out here get scared at the acts of the prophets and become podcast prophets: no more street teaching, nations can be saved, we love everybody. “Which are such things, as men can have nothing more profitable in their life”: there is nothing more profitable in your life than being courageous, wise and patient.

“If a man desire much experience, she knoweth things of old, and conjectureth aright what is to come”: she can figure out what is to come, the prophecies. “She knoweth the subtilties of speeches, and can expound dark sentences”: she can go into the Bible and bring out prophecies that people don't see though they are right there in front of them. “She foreseeth signs and wonders, and the events of seasons and times.”

Iran, the Arabs, the Israelis, the war: the bishops, the deacons and the captains bring it out in class all the time. We are foreseeing seasons and times. There is no time to sit around justifying multiple girlfriends; arguing about multiple vaginas is a child's game. We have grown folks' business to deal with.

“Therefore I purposed to take her to me to live with me, knowing that she would be a counsellor of good things, and a comfort in cares and grief.” That is why wisdom is called she: she is a companion like a wife, your comfort. And what did Christ call it? A comforter.

“For her sake I shall have estimation among the multitude, and honour with the elders, though I be young.” Solomon became king young, but he had honor because of the wisdom God gave him, and estimation among the elders who were before him and walked with David. “I shall be found of a quick conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of great men.” Over time people will begin to admire you because of the words of wisdom you teach out of this book.

“A man that hath travelled knoweth many things”: a man who leaves the country and goes out to search and seek his people. That is why the twelve tribes chart can expand now: when you travel and talk with our people scattered abroad outside of America, where there is little internet, understanding is added and expounded. The apostles got up off their behinds and traveled, and many of them died in their travels spreading the gospel outside their own boundaries.

“And he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” People in the comments saying God doesn't have a color show the level of brainwashing, whether heathen or heathen-minded Jake. That is why our warfare is not carnal: we are battling a spirit of divination, sorcery and witchcraft by which the heathen all conspire to keep our people in.

“He that hath no experience knoweth little”: he that doesn't travel anywhere doesn't know anything and can't be taken seriously as a leader. “But he that hath travelled is full of prudence”: full of wisdom and experience.
“When I travelled, I saw many things; and I understand more than I can express. I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things.”

Just before this, a sister was shown who had seen the march at the 2819 church: she heard us, saw us walking with authority and presence, was given a pamphlet, listened, and came to class that very morning. The word does not go out void. “He will keep the sayings of the renowned men: and where subtil parables are, he will be there also. He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables.”

“He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes”: he will have meetings with ambassadors, prime ministers, newscasts, public figures and activists. That is the work of a dynamic teacher; when you travel you come across people of interest. “He will travel through strange countries”: that is what Paul was doing.

“For he hath tried the good and the evil among men.” That is what was read earlier, having your senses exercised to discern good and evil. When you travel and gain experience, you are of full age.

“There is a man in thy kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of thy father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, was found in him.” Daniel had light, understanding and wisdom, and Nebuchadnezzar made him “master of the magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers”.

“Forasmuch as an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shewing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts, were found in the same Daniel.” When Daniel and the prophets spoke there was no I agree, I disagree, that's your opinion. They dissolved all doubts. What the Bible says is what it means; there is no you have your Bible version. You're just wrong, and it's okay to be wrong. “Now let Daniel be called, and he will shew the interpretation.”

precepts.why: What was that wisdom of the gods? “For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit”: it will not stay with you if you are deceitful. “And remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.” Who will not abide? The Father and his Son. They are the spirit of discipline that resides in us when we do the commandments and keep the sayings.

When you acquire this spirit, what spirit should you not have? “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power”: there's that word again. “And of love”: keeping commandments. “And of a sound mind.” All of those amount to one word: fortitude. Not fear, fortitude, and a readiness of mind.

As this truth progresses and people take notice of us, some Israelites will get fearful and turn into Christians and podcast prophets. After the Jersey shooting, when Muslims shot up a Jewish market and tried to blame us, some groups stopped wearing their fringes so they would not be associated. Now a camp leader complains that Israelites marched on a Christian event: leave them alone, they believe in Christ, go march on the Arabs. Which Christ do they believe in? These men lack fortitude. They have other nations in their camp and teach that the nations will be saved, and that emboldens them to speak against us. Make a decision; the Most High is going to separate the men from the boys.

sense.text:
Leave the Christians alone while they worship? “I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort.” Christ always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, and what were those? Religious gatherings. That is what Christ and the disciples did. So telling us to stay away from a religious gathering is telling Christ to mind his business.

That is cowardice, a lack of testicular fortitude: scary negroes afraid to piss off Massa because the job is good and they eat good, sleep good and live good. When a law like the one in France comes here and you can't teach Israel in the streets anymore, we'll see what you're made of. We won't stop.

Look at the black gatherings, MLK's, the Black Panthers', Occupy Wall Street, the George Floyd riots: who was among them? White folks, making sure the people didn't destroy their stores and neighborhoods. When black coffee is black it's strong and keeps you awake; put cream in it and it loses its effect. A lot of Israelite camps have coffee and cream all up in them and they're getting watered down and passive. Even outsiders in the comments said these are black men standing together, not violent, married and not just having baby mamas, out of jail and focused. People are seeing it.

For a lot of Israel, the Bible is something to do, not something to live, a way to pass the time. We are not going to sit in front of a computer screen talking about Christ's love and compassion; we have work to do. Christ provoked the elders and the disciples provoked the elders. The teaching itself is provocation: teaching that another kingdom is coming and America is going to be burned is provocation.

“Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled.” That is how they see us: hateful and ignorant men. “And they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.” They could tell by the way they taught that these were Christ's followers; they sounded just like their teacher, with boldness, bravery and power.

“Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name? and, behold, ye have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine”: the doctrine was spreading. “And intend to bring this man’s blood upon us”: you make us look bad.
“We ought to obey God rather than men.” We will obey God rather than men, and not scary, weak elders either.

“Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.” That is who Christ came for: his people, nobody else. So that Jesus they worship, the one we are told to leave alone, is not the Jesus of the Bible. We are done with Pastor Mitchell, but we will not stop attacking Christianity.
“And so is also the Holy Ghost, whom God hath given to them that obey him.” God gives you the Holy Spirit when you obey his words, his commandments, going back to John 14:15.

“When they heard that, they were cut to the heart, and took counsel to slay them.” The word of God came and cut them to the heart, the two-edged sword, and they wanted to kill them. That is provocation.

precepts.why:
“For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.” Your enemies will not be able to speak against it nor fight against it. That is Bible. And to have adversaries means you are going to provoke people.

What Bible are these camps reading, that say leave them alone? It's shocking to hear that come out of a man's mouth.

sense.text: “Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom”: wisdom, as Luke 21 said. “Whom we may appoint over this business”: appoint as deacons. “But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word.”
“They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost.” “And when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them.” Keep that in mind: when they prayed, they laid hands on them.
“And the word of God increased.” “And Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people.”

“Then there arose certain of the synagogue, which is called the synagogue of the Libertines, and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians”: one school, another school, another school. The elders of all these schools were disputing with Stephen. “And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake.” They could not refute what he was saying; the spirit was on him, and they could not deny what they saw and heard.

“Then they suborned men.” To suborn is to bribe or induce someone to commit an unlawful act such as perjury; from the Latin, to equip or incite secretly. They secretly equipped men with a lie: agents, spies even. They told these men what lie to tell on Stephen: “We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God.”
“And they stirred up the people”: they turned the people on Stephen and brought him to trial. “And set up false witnesses.” “This Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place”: and he will.

“And all that sat in the council, looking stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel.” The spirit of God was upon him; his body was as if illuminated, because power was coming from him.
“Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.” You always fight against the Holy Ghost, the same as your fathers did.

“Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One; of whom ye have been now the betrayers and murderers.” This is heavy. Your forefathers are the same men that killed the prophets who prophesied of Christ, and then you came and killed him. You are your fathers; you are your father, the devil. If you were an evil, cowardly negro back then, you will come back again and again and again. It doesn't change.
“Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it.” The law, the oracles, is the Holy Ghost of verse 51 that they rejected and refused to apply.

“When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth.” Stephen cut them with the word of God, and they were cursing him out. “But he, being full of the Holy Ghost”: and they ended up killing him.

Earlier the apostles laid hands on the seven men. “Then went up Moses, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.” Moses was our savior in this time. Moses, then Aaron, Nadab and Abihu: it is the same as the transfiguration, where Christ went up with Peter, James and John. And as in Luke, there was Christ, the top three, and the seventy disciples. Same thing, same order.
“And they saw the God of Israel”: they saw Christ. “And there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone.”

“And upon the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand”: he did not lay hands on them like they did in Acts. “Also they saw God, and did eat and drink.” They saw God too, because they were the elect, the chosen, that God dealt with. Not everyone saw this; only the men written here.

“Come up to me into the mount, and be there: and I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written; that thou mayest teach them.” On top of that mountain all Israel saw was a big fire, because they were blinded; Israel was evil as hell and turned to an idol. But these chosen men saw the Lord sitting there.
“And Moses rose up, and his minister Joshua.” In the New Testament, minister is deacon. So if Joshua was a deacon, what was Moses? A bishop. That is left there for another time.

“And Moses went out, and told the people the words of the Lord, and gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tabernacle.” These are the seventy men that saw God.

“And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy elders.” Now they all had the same spirit in them as Moses. “When the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease”: they began to teach and did not stop.

Eldad and Medad remained in the camp; the spirit rested on them too, “but went not out unto the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp.” A young man ran and told Moses, as if they were prophesying in the wrong place, and Joshua said, “My lord Moses, forbid them.” Stop them.

“Enviest thou for my sake?” Are you mad about that for me? “Would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them!” I wish the Lord would put his spirit upon all Israel to prophesy. Don't be mad about that.

That is what was seen at the blitz: brothers holding camp all over the sidewalk, teaching a family here, giving out flyers and explaining them there, captains here, the bishop here, deacons here, officers here, all saying the exact same things in different ways and teaching the exact same doctrine. No blue shirt, red shirt, do-rag, fitted hat: order, structure, uniformity. No schisms over here.
“And Moses gat him into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.” Moses went where those men were, and the elders of Israel went with him.

“Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing.” That cannot be done without elders; you need elders, guidance and leadership to teach you how to do that.

“And that there be no divisions among you.” There are no divisions here. When something is brought out differently, it was discussed first. The Bishop brings something out, the deacons come after him, and if anything is different it was already discussed: bring that out, don't bring that out yet, we'll go over that later. That is leadership, checks and balances. We don't operate like orphans.

“But that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment”: the same spirit. At the blitz the Christian cult members went from camp to camp to find a flaw, and they came to say, you're going to say so and so, because they heard it at the other camp. All praises: we are all saying the exact same thing. They tried to find a kink in the army and couldn't.

precepts.why: “So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man.” This is how we were: knit together as one man, one spirit, no schisms. That is what they saw out there at the 2819 church: all of us teaching the exact same things in different ways, the same breakdowns. That is what elders, leadership, guidance and years of experience and exercise produce.
“Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be likeminded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind.” Of one accord, of one mind: knit as one man. The same thing, nothing new.

sense.text: “As he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel”: Christ taught at a religious gathering. He was provoking, stirring the pot. “The chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders”, saying, “Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?” Who told you that you could teach here? Who do you work for?

“I will also ask you one thing; and answer me: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?” The teaching of John, was it of heaven or of man? They had to huddle. If they said from heaven, he would ask why they did not believe him; if they said of men, the people would stone them, “for they be persuaded that John was a prophet”: John had a huge following. So they answered “that they could not tell whence it was.” “Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things”: if you can't answer my question, I'm not answering yours. That's a black man right there.

“A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.” The vineyard is us. The husbandmen are the servants, the leaders and elders of the people, and he left us to their leadership.

“At the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.” The servant is the prophet sent to collect for the Lord. The elders beat another, as they did Jeremiah, and wounded a third and cast him out.

“I will send my beloved son: it may be they will reverence him when they see him.” Perhaps when they see my son, whom they know is my son, they will treat him with more respect than the servants before.

“This is the heir: come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.” This is the son of God, the heir to all of this; let's kill him, and then we can lead the people forever. They knew who he was and didn't care. They wanted his position: if we kill him, he can't reign over us, and we reign over all the people. So they cast him out and had him crucified.

“He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others”: he shall come and kill them all and give the vineyard to righteous Israelite elders, real leaders. “And when they heard it, they said, God forbid.” See how evil these Jake were.

“What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?” According to prophecy, the elders get replaced by the stone. “Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken”: whoever attacks or kills that stone shall be destroyed. “But on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.” Christ is saying: you are going to kill me, and I am going to come back and kill you.

“And the chief priests and the scribes the same hour sought to lay hands on him; and they feared the people: for they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them.” They got what he was saying. A dynamic teacher can insult anyone without saying their name or mentioning their group: he brings the word of God out, it cuts their hearts, and they know he is talking about them.

“And they watched him”: they watch his videos today. “And sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.” A camp boasts of having moles in ours. That shows who these men are today: the same men that killed Christ and the disciples, in bed with the white man. Like the Pharisees, they are captives who desire king privileges, so they would kill the heir and rule in the white man's pocket forever. Nothing different.

precepts.why: “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” That is where Christ is quoting from. The chief priests said God forbid, and Christ answered them with what was already written.

Where does Christ get falling on the stone and being broken? “Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” That Lord in verse 13 is the Son. “And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel”: a rock of provocation, of offense, to Judah and Ephraim, “for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.”

“And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.” That is the stone of Luke 20: those who fall on it and those it falls on. Christ is saying he will come back and kill them.

sense.text: “For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee.” Christ came out of the Father.

“Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me.” There is an elect group of Israelites who are Christ's children, and the rest are evil negroes that are going to be destroyed. “That they may be one, as we are.” So what happened to Christ also applies to his children, because the Father and the Son are one, and we are one with our father, Christ.

“That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee.” “And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them.” Christ was put to death and received into glory, and so will his children be, because of provocation. “That they may be made perfect in one”: knit as one man, no schism, no division.
“Father, I will that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory.”

“And there was much murmuring among the people concerning him”: concerning Christ, and concerning us at the 2819 church. “For some said, He is a good man”: these guys are doing a good thing. “Others said, Nay; but he deceiveth the people”: they're full of hate, they teach hate. “Howbeit no man spake openly of him for fear of the Jews”: for fear of their pastor.

Some said, “Of a truth this is the Prophet”, others, “This is the Christ”, and some, “Shall Christ come out of Galilee?” “So there was a division among the people because of him. And some of them would have taken him; but no man laid hands on him”, because many believed and some did not.

“Why have ye not brought him?” Why haven't you arrested him? “The officers answered, Never man spake like this man”: no man taught like him before. “Are ye also deceived?” Are you being brainwashed too?

Nicodemus, “he that came to Jesus by night”, was Christ's secret disciple. “Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?” At least hear him out first. “Art thou also of Galilee?” As if Galilee were the ghetto: “for out of Galilee ariseth no prophet.”
The blind man Christ healed. His neighbors asked, “How were thine eyes opened?” “A man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes”, and he went and washed, and received sight.

“And it was the sabbath day when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.” Some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not of God, because he keepeth not the sabbath day.” Others said, “How can a man that is a sinner do such miracles? And there was a division among them.” Division among the people, again, because of him.

Men like Pastor Pam are not new. “But there was a certain man, called Simon, which beforetime in the same city used sorcery”: Christianity. “And bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one”: he speaks against the other pastors, but he is no better than them, and now he is some great one.

“To whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest”: fifty thousand standing in line listening to him. “Saying, This man is the great power of God”: this man is a great pastor of God. “And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries.”
“But Elymas the sorcerer”: another sorcerer like Simon. He “withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith”, as they stand against us.

“Then Saul, (who also is called Paul,) filled with the Holy Ghost, set his eyes on him”, and said to this wicked pastor, “O full of all subtilty and all mischief, thou child of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?”

These pastors are nothing new. We will prophesy again, and all these wicked pastors and wicked elders we will deal with as the Bible tells us to. The weapons of our warfare are not carnal.
